checked.claim: A hindering Call armed more than 60 s before is thrown and spent on the supporting rolls pickCover, tailUnseen and lootCover on the primary, while the roller's window shields it, so an honest roll is flagged and the Call is gone before the action's own roll.
checked.why: Read the whole road. rollTrait shields every `remember: false` roll outside TAKES_CALLS, which holds murderOpening alone, so the roller's pendingCalls answers [] and the window and packet carry no Call. The three callers pass `remember: false` with an action key. On the primary throwDrawn takes the key as sent (regex check only); SPENDS_NO_CALL holds "palm" alone, so `applied` is read normally (empty: the packet names none) and hostileCalls, whose early return covers only SPENDS_NO_CALL and a keyless claimed roll, returns every hindering Call armed before HOSTILE_GRACE, read through armedCallsShown, which has no shield test. expectedFor adds read.hostile.dice and .bonus into the GM's number, checkRoll flags `advantage` or `modifier` for the difference, and `used = [...applied, ...hostile]` spends them. traitsFor names pickCover, tailUnseen and lootCover as drawn keys, and the bridge binds these rolls by those kinds, so the draw road is the one these rolls take. The comment over SPENDS_NO_CALL says it mirrors rollTrait's `remember: false`, which it no longer does. No test found that pins the opposite: tests-tier2.mjs's pickCover/tailUnseen rows (101614, 102481, 103069) build rolls through rollOf without an armed hindering Call, and the hostileCalls tests (9814, 9862, 10009) drive action rolls. Minor holds: it needs a hindering Call standing at the moment of one of three actions, and it costs that Call and raises a false flag.

checked.claim: With the roll window lock off, a player's ticked Experience, typed bonus or other statistic is shown in the window but not counted by the GM's draw, so the roll is flagged and the roller told 'not counted'; the setting's text describes only the on state.
checked.why: The lock-off branch of roll-dialog leaves the trait, the experience chips and a bonus no Call set to the player (freeBonus). On the primary the `experience` reader answers its bound only when an applied Call grants `experience`, scoredOf slices the claim's experiences to that bound and clamps the rest of the flat sum into the effects' range, and checkRoll flags `modifier` when the claim's flat differs or holds more experiences, `trait` when the statistic differs from the action's. rollerLine then names `uncounted` to the roller. Nothing in roll-draw reads lockRollDialog (grep finds the setting only in roll-dialog.mjs:551, settings.mjs and settings-window.mjs:91), so the draw does not change its count with the switch. The tier-2 test at tests-tier2.mjs:75180-75230 opens an unlocked window and clicks an experience chip, but it reads the window's costs and Roll button, not what the GM counts. One narrowing: the title's 'counts none of them' is wide - a typed bonus within the character's effects' range is counted - but what_happens says so (the clamp). Minor holds: the default is on.

checked.claim: A player's diagnoseDiceLook() with no message id reads the newest message with rolls whose `visible` is not false, which includes another player's hidden whispered roll, and prints its author and its dice kinds in the window the player is asked to send the GM.
checked.why: rollMessage filters a player's run by `m.visible !== false` only. The module's own note states that Foundry's ChatMessage#visible answers true for any whispered message holding a roll, and the module hides such cards through isContentVisible alone (enforceContentVisibility returns early only on isContentVisible); the harness models visible that way. The module patches isContentVisible (readableRule) and nothing patches ChatMessage#visible (grep of `get visible` and `"visible"` over scripts/ finds only fog-doorways' ruler). lookView then sets `by = message.author?.id` without the GM-only branch, and viewLines prints `Roll: <name> - <dice>`; the same view feeds diceLookLines, the diagnostic report's part on a player's browser too (diagnostics.mjs:2227). The dice lines carry class, faces and modifiers, not the faces rolled, so the leak is who rolled and with which dice, as the finding says. Foundry's own getter was not read here (not on this machine); the claim rests on the module's note and the harness's model, as the reader says. Minor holds: the player must run a diagnostic, and it shows that a hidden roll was made and by whom.

checked.claim: On the primary every actor flag write below full Gamemaster schedules a dice-look put-back and the switches' comparison whether or not it touches Dice So Nice's flags.
checked.why: The road is as read: the updateActor hook passes touchesLook, and below full Gamemaster onActorWritten ignores `touched` and calls afterSwitchesHeld. But it is narrower than said and the 'expected' is not safe as written. Narrower: registerDiceSync adds the hook only with Dice So Nice active; afterSwitchesHeld runs the step (and so the 400 ms timer and the put-back) only while the table's look is forced (`enforcing()`); worldCopyMoved stringifies only on a full Gamemaster's primary. Not safe: touchesLook tests `Object.hasOwn(flags, DSN)`, so a write that removes the whole namespace with the legacy `-=dice-so-nice` key (which 14.370 still honours, CLAUDE.md, LIVE-E30-01) does not carry the `dice-so-nice` key and reads as untouched; the unconditional schedule is what catches it below full Gamemaster. The reader's refutation says any write of the overlay carries the key, which this form does not. The cost remains unmeasured. Nit holds.
